name: correctness

findings.message: `zbuild_claim_release` never unsets `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`, so a second invocation is not a no-op as the design requires.
findings.quote:
# Only release if this process acquired the claim
    [[ -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}" ]] && return 0

    # Remove zbuild:claimed (advisory; failures never abort the run)
    _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "zbuild:claimed" || true

    return 0
findings.trigger: The design document for this issue states: 'unsets `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` before calling `_ccgl_remove_label` (advisory). Unsetting first makes a second call a no-op.' Because `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` is never unset inside the function, any second call that arrives while the variable still holds `"1"` will pass the guard and invoke `_ccgl_remove_label` again on an already-removed label. In production the gh call returns non-zero (label absent), but `|| true` silences it; in the local-fs backend `grep -Fxv` on the already-cleaned file writes an empty replacement and succeeds silently. DSCLA-13 is not affected today because `trap '' TERM` in `_runner_abort_trap` prevents re-entry, but the idempotency guarantee the design chose is absent from the function itself.

knocked_down.message: `claim_coordinator_claim` and `claim_coordinator_release` still use the per-machine label `claimed:<machine>` that the issue required to be replaced with `zbuild:claimed`, and the unit test at lines 44–49 asserts the old label pattern and passes, masking the unimplemented change.
knocked_down.trigger: The unit test calls `claim_coordinator_claim "42"` (line 33) and then asserts `grep -q "claimed:" "$labels_file"` (line 45). `claimed:<machine>` is written instead of `zbuild:claimed`. If another run on a different machine checks for `zbuild:claimed` (as `zbuild_claim_acquire` does via `grep -Fxq "zbuild:claimed"`), it will not see the per-machine label and both runs will proceed concurrently — the exact cross-machine collision the issue was designed to prevent (RQLAB-1, RQLAB-2). The corresponding `claim_coordinator_release` removes `claimed:${machine}`, so it also would not remove the `zbuild:claimed` label added by `zbuild_claim_acquire`. The test at lines 44–49 would fail if the function were correctly changed, so it currently passes while enforcing the unfixed state.
knocked_down.why: The engine's runner.sh calls `zbuild_claim_acquire` (not `claim_coordinator_claim`) for the cross-machine claim; `zbuild_claim_acquire` writes and checks `zbuild:claimed` on both machines, so two concurrent runs correctly exclude each other without ever touching `claim_coordinator_claim`.

reason: the correctness lens found a medium or high or critical problem the change introduced
